chunks: From him, and from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad together, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said: I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

Every Muslim born between two Muslim parents who apostatizes from Islam, denies Muḥammad and his prophethood, and declares him false—then his blood is lawful for everyone who hears that from him; his wife is separated from him from the day he apostatized, so she must not approach him; his wealth is divided among his heirs; his wife observes the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died; and it is upon the Imam to kill him and not seek his repentance.

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which the person apostatized
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the legitimate authority responsible for carrying out the ruling
key_terms.دَمَهُ مُبَاحٌ: his blood is licit; legal immunity from retaliation is removed
key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: the waiting period observed by a widow after her husband's death
key_terms.نُبُوَّتَهُ: his prophethood; the prophetic mission of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.وَرَثَتِهِ: his heirs who inherit his property

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about the ruling on apostasy and its legal consequences?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning a Muslim born to two Muslim parents who apostatizes by denying the prophethood of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It outlines the legal consequences affecting blood liability, marriage, inheritance, and the Imam’s judicial duty in such a case.
